title: Derived tensor and open restriction in independent universes
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and U an arbitrary open. Give D(O_X) and D(O_U) independently chosen localizations [def-pc-derived-category] and the derived tensor [def-pc-scheme-derived-tensor-structure]. For arbitrary E,F in D(O_X), exact restriction R (the over functor followed by the over equivalence) satisfies R(E tensor-derived F) is isomorphic to R(E) tensor-derived R(F). No quasi-coherence or boundedness hypothesis is required.

source.place: Lemma 36.3.9, proof of (1), locality and the K-flat computation (2); Tag 08DV for tilde K-flatness

proof.text: Represent E,F by Q(M),Q(N) using essential surjectivity of Q. Resolve M by a K-flat P with quasi-isomorphism s:P→M. Q(s) and the representative comparison give eP:Q(P)≅E and eN:Q(N)≅F. Evaluate the existing natural K-flat tensor comparison on constant singleton families to obtain a:Q(P) tensor Q(N)≅Q(Tot(P tensor N)).

Restriction of P is K-flat. Compute the tensor of Q(R(P)) and Q(R(N)) in the independently chosen derived category on U by the same existing K-flat tensor comparison. The total tensor restriction isomorphism identifies R(Tot(P tensor N)) with Tot(R(P) tensor R(N)).

Use mapDerivedCategoryFactors to identify RD(Q(C)) with Q(R(C)) for each complex C. Compose RD(tensorIso(eP,eN).symm), RD(a), the factors comparison at Tot(P tensor N), Q of the total tensor restriction isomorphism, the inverse target K-flat comparison, the inverse tensor of the factors comparisons at P,N, and tensorIso(RD(eP),RD(eN)). This proves the unchanged statement with independent localization universes. No cross-universe monoidal localization equivalence is needed.
